title: Customer feedback DNA decompilation and probe kits
content:
Quick note: this is a working synthesis — aimed at turning repeated, messy customer threads into small, testable probe kits for eng+product. Not polished; contains hypothesis-driven asks and low-effort experiments we can run within 2–4 sprints.

Topline summary:
- Signal: multiple mid-market customers report surprising token-level cost spikes when using chat flows with long histories + system prompts. They surface this as both bill shock and unpredictable latency outliers.
- Root hypothesis: a combination of suboptimal prefix trimming, no-op KV-cache misses across model variants, and conservative batching configuration yields both higher token cost and intermittent 2–5x latency tail events for certain workloads.
- Priority: low-effort mitigations that reduce cost-variance and the high-latency tail without changing model outputs (customer-facing behavior).

Representative vignettes (anonymized):
1) "Retail-ML" (Large commerce customer): chat assistant used for returns triage; payloads include product metadata and multi-turn conversation history. They observed a 3x cost increase over a month when a specific agent team started including raw image captions in system prompts. They want a way to limit or warn about high-cost prompt constructs.
2) "Data-Insights" (analytics SaaS): heavy use of embeddings + retriever-augmented generation (RAG). Their evaluation showed repeated full-kv-cache flushes on model switch during canary rollouts, causing latency spikes and failed SLAs for synchronous web requests.
3) "FinReg" (regulated customer): runs on Redwood Private; tolerates slower throughput but needs absolutely predictable upper-bound latency for audit windows. They want a conservative, cost-aware fallback policy that never returns a higher-cost model variant without explicit opt-in.

Extracted asks (clustered):
- Ask A: Prompt-level cost guardrails (warn/auto-trim long system prompts; show estimated token cost pre-send). Engineering effort: small (console + API flag + simple estimate lib). Product impact: high (reduces bill shock).
- Ask B: KV-cache continuity across model variant rollouts (avoid full flush on compatible-variant fallback). Engineering effort: medium (runtime routing + cache key stability tests). Product impact: medium-high (reduces latency tail).
- Ask C: Tail-latency hedging policy (route riskier requests to capacity with higher isolation or apply short-circuit fallback to smaller quantized variants when tail triggers). Engineering effort: medium-high (policy layer + telemetry). Product impact: high for SLAs.
- Ask D: Cost-annotated webhooks for customers to see token estimates for each callback (developer UX). Effort: small.

Probe kit suggestions (experiments we can run quickly):
- Probe 1 (2 weeks): "Prompt-cost-tracker" feature flag on Hosted: compute token estimate client-side in SDK and surface a non-blocking warning if estimated cost > baseline. Track whether customers reduce prompt length. Metrics: number of warnings, change in avg tokens per request, conversion (do they still send?). Linked test ticket: JIRA-CS-1823.
- Probe 2 (3 sprints): "Cache-stability-canary": on Dedicated clusters, implement a compatibility shim that keeps KV-cache keys stable across 3 model-variant transitions and run A/B with a small percent of traffic. Measure KV-cache hit-rate, tail latency, and error rates. Linked ticket: JIRA-ENG-5530.
- Probe 3 (1 month): "Tail-hedge-policy" – introduce a runtime rule that detects 95th percentile token generation > Xms and routes subsequent in-flight similar requests to quantized-small variant for 5 mins. Run on a staging region and audit deviation in outputs for sample prompts.

Metrics to capture for each probe (minimum):
- per-request token estimate vs actual tokens billed
- KV-cache hit/miss rate and time-to-first-token
- 50/90/95/99 latency percentiles pre/post
- customer-reported bill anomalies (CS tickets)

Engineering notes / feasibility quick hits:
- Prompt cost estimates: reuse existing tokenizer + model-length heuristics in SDK; surface as advisory. No server-side changes required for MVP.
- KV-cache stability: largest risk is cache key leakage across tenants and variant mismatches — need unit tests + canary config. Consider a toggle per-customer.
- Hedging policy: requires per-request lightweight classifier (heuristic based on prompt length + model family + historical tail). Could be rule-based initially.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How acceptable is small divergence in outputs when hedging to quantized variants? Need .eval prompt sets from customers to judge quality delta.
- Do we surface cost warnings only in Console/SDK or block via API? Default advisory preferred to avoid breaking apps.
- For Private customers, who owns rollout of cache-stability shim (Redwood ops + customer infra)? Document the installation path.

Recommended immediate next steps (owners and timeline):
- Next 1 week: ship client-side prompt-cost advisory prototype in JS SDK (owner: Maya Chen, CS). Collect early signals.
- Next 2 weeks: run internal experiment instrumenting KV-cache hit rates during a planned model-variant swap (owner: Diego Ramirez, Eng/Serving-runtime).
- 1 month: assemble small eval pack (5–10 prompts per affected customer) to quantify output divergence for quantized variants (owner: Liam O'Connor, Product).

Notes to follow up in next brainstorm session:
- Collect a short list of customers willing to participate in canaries (asking them for eval prompt sets and SLA windows).
- Design a minimal Console UI for cost advisory with an opt-out for advanced teams.

Raw links / references (for running experiments):
- Confluence signal index: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Signal+Index+2026
- Ticket for prompt-cost-tracker: JIRA-CS-1823
- Eng ticket for cache shim: JIRA-ENG-5530
- Ops PR with hedging policy prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-proposals/pull/87

Quick sign-off checklist for CS -> Eng handoff: 
- [ ] provide anonymized sample prompts and representative traffic shapes
- [ ] define acceptance criteria for each probe (latency reduction thresholds, cost reduction % targets)
- [ ] confirm storage/telemetry retention needed for analysis (30 days min)

Notes-to-self: when drafting the JS SDK advisory, keep the copy non-alarming ("estimated token units") and include link to docs about how estimates are computed.

End of working doc.
